amendments.rule: **A numeral phrase may hold more waws than the ASV renders.** Align the ASV's *and* to the waw standing between the same two numerals the English *and* stands between, and mark any other waw in the phrase `unrepresented`. In `חָמֵשׁ וְתִשְׁעִים שָׁנָה וּשְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה` → *eight hundred ninety and five years* the English *and* joins ninety to five, so the units-to-tens waw takes it and the waw at the group boundary has nothing; in `תְּשַׁע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה` → *nine hundred and thirty years* the same English *and* joins the two groups, so there the group-boundary waw is the one that takes it. This is determined rather than a tie-break: the ASV's *and* stands between specific numerals, so read which, rather than preferring a position. **The surplus runs the other way just as often.** Where the phrase holds more English *and*s than waws, an *and* standing between two numerals no waw joins is `added` under rule 30, because no morpheme licenses it: `מֵאָה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר` → *a hundred and twelve*, `אֶלֶף שִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר` → *a thousand and seventeen*, `שְׁמֹנֶה מֵאוֹת שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר` → *eight hundred and eighteen*, `אַרְבַּע רִבּוֹא אַלְפַּיִם` → *forty and two thousand*. Do not fold such an *and* into a neighbouring numeral's unit to avoid the `added`: rule 30's fusion wants one English word, and this *and* is written beside the numerals rather than inside one of them. Count the waws, count the *and*s, and set them against each other by the pair of numerals each stands between; whichever side is in surplus is what the two halves of this rule dispose of. An ASV italic on such an *and* corroborates it, and the absence of one is not evidence against it, by rule 7.
amendments.why: Rule 42 as written considers only the waw-surplus direction, and a census chapter produces the mirror case as readily: NEH.7 has four numeral figures whose ASV writes an *and* where the Hebrew has no waw (vv.11, 24, 42, 66) against three whose Hebrew has a waw the ASV does not write (vv.37, 62, 67). Left one-directional, the rule sends a later pass to rule 30's fusion clause, which would wrongly absorb the surplus *and* into an adjacent numeral's unit. The corpus does not contradict: its teen numerals are single English words (*fourteen*, *fifteen*, *seventeen*) and `מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים` → *sixscore*, so no surplus *and* arises there to be counted against this. The italic clause is included because NEH.7.24's surplus *and* carries no italic markup while vv.11, 42 and 66 do.

conventions: A construct chain whose ASV rendering carries a single *the* at the phrase's left edge gives that *the* to an article morpheme present anywhere in the chain, including one standing on a second, coordinated nomen rectum that the ASV renders bare: `אַנְשֵׁי בֵית אֵל וְהָעָי` → *The men of Beth el and Ai* (v.32) puts the *The* on הָעָי's article and leaves אַנְשֵׁי with *men* alone, exactly as `אַנְשֵׁי הָרָמָה וָגָבַע` → *The men of Ramah and Geba* does in v.30. Supply a *the* on the construct only where no article morpheme stands in the chain at all (vv.33-34 `אַנְשֵׁי נְבוֹ אַחֵר`, v.39 `בֵית יֵשׁוּעַ`, v.60 `בְנֵי עַבְדֵי שְׁלֹמֹה`), and mark an article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all (v.2 `אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים` → *God*, v.65 `הַכֹּהֵן` → *a priest*).

רִבּוֹא is fused or split by how many English words the ASV spends on it, not by the construction. `אַרְבַּע רִבּוֹא` → *forty* (v.66) meets rule 30's one-English-word condition and is one unit headed on the counting numeral; `שְׁתֵּי רִבּוֹא`/`רִבּוֹת` → *twenty thousand* (vv.71, 72) does not, so rule 2 splits it, the counting numeral taking *twenty* and the multiplier noun taking *thousand*.

In a verbless enumeration clause the supplied copula joins the numeral the English copula stands before, not a head noun standing later in the predicate: *were three hundred* (v.60), *there were seven thousand* (v.67), *were seven hundred* (v.68), and *was twenty thousand darics of gold* (v.72), where *was* goes to שְׁתֵּי and דַּרְכְּמוֹנִים keeps *darics*.

An ASV italic joins the unit of the morpheme whose sense it spells out, and is `added` only where no morpheme carries that sense. *houses* in `רָאשֵׁי הָאָבוֹת` → *the heads of fathers houses* (vv.70, 71) joins הָאָבוֹת, which in this idiom names the ancestral houses, and heads on *fathers* by rule 31; *their* before the absolute `גְּמַלִּים` and `חֲמֹרִים` (v.69) answers to no suffix and is `added`, as is the *and* of a numeral figure that holds no waw (vv.11, 24, 42, 66) — v.24's is not italicised, and that is not evidence against it (rule 7).

report: Read all 52 candidate groups and the whole dump end to end (the table is blind to `added`, and this chapter holds 8 such units). Two real splits found; everything else is difference the source licenses.

Split 1 - the fronted *The* of a construct chain. The chapter's settled treatment is that a present article morpheme takes the single *the* the ASV writes for the phrase, and the construct takes nothing: v.6 שְׁבִי הַגּוֹלָה, v.30 הָרָמָה, v.65 קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, v.66 כָּל הַקָּהָל, vv.70-71 רָאשֵׁי הָאָבוֹת. NEH.7.32 alone supplied the *The* on אַנְשֵׁי and marked הָעָי's article `unrepresented`, reasoning from 'no *the* for the place name' - the exact reading v.30's review note records as corrected ('the clause turns on no *the* for the phrase'). The only source difference is that the arthrous name is the second, coordinated rectum, and rule 29 does not condition on that. Patched v.32.

Split 2 - the copula of a verbless enumeration clause. vv.60, 67 and 68 put it on the numeral the English copula stands before (*were three hundred*, *there were seven thousand*, *were seven hundred*); NEH.7.72 alone put it on a head noun three words later (*was* ... *darics*), which its own note flagged as contested. The corpus reads numeral predicates the first way throughout - מֵאָה gives *was a hundred* in 13 units, beside *was forty*, *were forty*, *was five*, *was seven*, *was six*, *was threescore*, *was fifty* - and never moves the copula off the numeral. Patched v.72; the unit is now contiguous.

BSB: of the 8 disagreements exactly one is a genuine error - v.32 הָ, fixed above on Hebrew grounds and not on BSB's account (rule 38). The other seven are documented convention differences: v.2 הָאֱלֹהִים and v.65 הַכֹּהֵן have no ASV *the* to take (*feared God*, *a priest*); v.5 וָ is silenced by the ASV's infinitive recasting and v.37/v.67 וְ by rule 42's waw surplus; v.5 ה is a cohortative he (rule 32); v.61 לְ is bare after a modal (rules 40, 52). No accepted edge was moved to improve the rate.

Checked and left alone: the four Td→Vqrmpa substantival articles (vv.5, 6, 7, 61) differ only in how much antecedent the ASV writes; שִׁיר as *singers* (vv.1, 73) against *singing men/women* (v.67) is the ASV distinguishing sexes; עָלָה *went up* (v.6) against *were ... went up* (v.61), where rule 41's predicate keeps its copula; the four `added` numeral *and*s (vv.11, 24, 42, 66) all stand where no waw does, and the three `unrepresented` waws (vv.37, 62, 67) all stand where no *and* does, so rule 42 and its mirror are applied consistently; v.64's `added` *among* against v.67's folded *of whom*, which the demonstrative's own appositional function licenses; v.69's `added` *their* against vv.70-71's folded *houses*, recorded as a convention.

One contestable single-occurrence reading left standing: v.73 הַחֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִי → *the seventh month* gives the *the* to the noun's article and marks the attributive's `unrepresented`. Rule 47's headline ('the first article takes it') supports that, but its test ('read which word the ASV's *the* stands before') points the other way once English fronts the ordinal. The chapter has no second instance, so I did not disturb it or write a rule on it.
